Each entry preserves the historical boundary and last admitted predecessor. Git path, regular-file mode, commit and bytes are checked; any later byte change rejects until a new reviewed owner admits it. The report's `source_image_evolutions` names actual current images. Older inverse/falsifier rows explicitly name their preserved predecessor `source_stage`; those original controls and all original results remain. For example, the historical ZIP can still recover every selected input while a later Compiler edit causes `unreviewed current source image: perl/LinkedSpec/Compiler.pm`. Restoring the admitted current image passes; refreshing an old historical hash is never the repair. The new path-wise current-image mutations exercise that rejection, while original-log reads and tracked writes remain denied. Source identity admission does not re-execute old runtime producers or promote feature/objective compatibility; that verification remains deferred under its existing owners.
